public_summary: Iran's internet remains in partial outage with no material change since the last pass 20 minutes ago. All foreign platforms (Google, Telegram, YouTube, Instagram, WhatsApp, GitHub) and most domestic services (Digikala, Aparat, Tapsi, Filimo, CafeBazaar) remain accessible. All ISP management gateways continue to block inbound probes, and Iranian IP range reachability from outside holds at approximately 3.2%. Circumvention tools (Tor, Snowflake, Psiphon) remain accessible. Saman Bank shows slight latency improvement but remains degraded.
insight: The near-identical fingerprint across consecutive passes — zero ISP gateways reachable, 3.2% IP range reachability, all foreign platforms working, all circumvention tools accessible — confirms this is Iran's sustained anti-monitoring posture rather than any transient disruption; the network edge remains intentionally opaque to external probes while user-facing traffic flows normally, and the only micro-change (Saman Bank latency dropping ~500ms) suggests routine load fluctuation rather than a policy shift.
recommendation: This stable pattern across multiple passes represents a confirmed operational baseline for Iran's anti-monitoring infrastructure. Shift monitoring focus to detection of deviation: a sudden improvement in IP range reachability or gateway responsiveness could signal a policy relaxation, while any foreign platform outage would indicate escalation into user-facing censorship. Cross-reference with IODA traffic volume trends for TIC (AS12880) and consider adding a traceroute probe to distinguish between routing-level blocking and application-layer filtering at the gateways.
